To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dinuclear complexes of Pd(II) and Pt(II) ions with the N,N,N', N'-tetrakis (2-pyridylethyl) benzene-1, 4-diamine ligand are promising candidates for the development of new drugs with antitumour properties.

the dinuclear platinum complexes with the N,N,N′,N′-tetrakis(4-pyridyl)methyl)benzylamine ligand exhibit higher DNA-binding ability than the mononuclear complexes, and the cytotoxicity of dinuclear platinum complexes is more effective on cancer cells.

the dinuclear platinum and palladium complexes are able to interact with DNA and BSA, while the cytotoxic effect of dinuclear platinum complex PP2 is higher than the cytotoxic effect exerted by cisplatin and the mononuclear platinum complex.

the synthesis and characterization of homo- and hetero- dinuclear Pt(II) and Pd(II) coordination complexes.
the design of new metal-based compounds with promising antitumor properties.

the synthesis, characterization, hydrolysis and substitution reactions, DNA and BSA interactions, DFT and molecular docking studies, as well as the cytotoxic activity of three new dinuclear complexes.
